hook.text: A printer lays down living cells layer by layer — building tissue structures that no mold could ever shape.

buildup.text: Bio-inks combine cells with hydrogels — the gel supports cells during printing while they organize into tissue.

discovery.text: Extrusion, inkjet, and laser-based printing each offer different resolution and cell viability trade-offs.

twist.text: Printed tissue thicker than 200 μm dies without blood vessels — vascularization is the unsolved grand challenge.

climax.text: Researchers printed ear cartilage, skin grafts, and bone patches — clinical trials are beginning for simple tissues.

punchline.text: Printing organs is the dream — viable tissues are today's frontier.

quiz.question: What is the biggest challenge for bioprinting thick tissues?
options: Cells cannot survive the printing process
Tissue beyond 200 μm thick dies without vascular networks to supply nutrients
